name: Budget Buddy — the project you build
summary: One small program that grows as you learn. Budget Buddy is a money tracker that runs in your terminal. It starts by asking for your income and one expense, and ends as a menu-driven app that stores expenses, groups them into categories, reports on your spending, and saves everything to a file. Each phase adds one layer using the ideas you just learned. You never throw the code away.

stages.title: Ask and calculate
stages.goal: Use variables, numbers, strings and user input to work out what is left of your money.
deliverables: A budget-buddy folder created with npm init
prompt-sync installed as a dependency
Asks for your name, monthly income and three expenses
Prints a neat summary with the money left over, to two decimal places

stages.title: Warnings and checks
stages.goal: Make the program react: warn when you overspend, and reject nonsense input.
deliverables: Rejects amounts that are not numbers or are negative
Warns when expenses are more than income
Shows a status message (healthy / tight / overspent) based on what is left

stages.title: Keep going until I quit
stages.goal: Replace the fixed three expenses with a loop, so you can add as many as you like.
deliverables: A menu loop: add expense, show total, quit
Keeps a running total and a count
Tracks the biggest single expense
Keeps asking until the input is valid

stages.title: Tidy it into functions
stages.goal: Break the growing program into small, named, reusable functions.
deliverables: formatMoney, askForAmount, showMenu and statusFor functions
At least two arrow functions
The main loop reads almost like plain English

stages.title: Remember every expense
stages.goal: Store the amounts in an array so you can list and analyse them.
deliverables: Expenses stored in an array
A menu option that lists every expense with its number
Remove an expense by its number
Average and largest expense worked out with loops you wrote

stages.title: Real records, saved to disk
stages.goal: Turn each expense into an object with a description, amount and category, and save them to a file.
deliverables: Expenses are objects: { description, amount, category }
Totals per category
Data saved to budget.json and loaded when the program starts

stages.title: Reports
stages.goal: Use array methods to build useful reports in a few clear lines.
deliverables: Filter expenses by category
Top 3 biggest expenses, sorted
Category totals using reduce
Search expenses by a word in the description

stages.title: Finished and organised
stages.goal: Split the program into modules, fix any bugs, track it in Git, and write a README.
deliverables: Code split into files: storage.js, money.js, reports.js, index.js
An npm start script
A Git repository with meaningful commits
A README explaining how to run it
